```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

rm(list = ls())

# installs (if missing) and loads every package this project uses - add any
# new packages to scripts/00-packages.R, not here
source("../scripts/00-packages.R")

# downloads the data into data/raw/ if you don't already have it, then loads
# eindscores, referentieniveaus, schooladviezen and schoolweging into this
source("../scripts/01-get-data.R")
```


```{r prepare-data}

#Select relevant reference-level variables
count_cols <- c("REKENEN_LAGER1F", "REKENEN_1F", "REKENEN_1S",
                "LV_LAGER1F", "LV_1F", "LV_2F")

# value for DUO's "<5" (1-4 pupils): the midpoint
lt5_value <- 2.5

replace_lt5 <- function(x) {
  x <- as.character(x)
  as.numeric(if_else(x == "<5", as.character(lt5_value), x))
}

#Convert columns to numeric, and turn values like <5 to NA
#Clean reference-level counts
ref_levels <- referentieniveaus |>
  mutate(across(all_of(count_cols), replace_lt5)) |> #used to turn <5 into NA, now into 2.5 to prevent false 100$ scores? For small schools, this quite greatly influenced averages for example. 
  group_by(INSTELLINGSCODE) |>
  summarise(
    GEMEENTENAAM = first(GEMEENTENAAM),
    INSTELLINGSNAAM_VESTIGING = first(INSTELLINGSNAAM_VESTIGING),
    across(all_of(count_cols), ~ sum(.x, na.rm = TRUE)), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(
    #total number of students for maths and for reading
    rekenen_n = REKENEN_LAGER1F + REKENEN_1F + REKENEN_1S,
    reading_n = LV_LAGER1F + LV_1F + LV_2F,
    #percentage of students for each level
    math_1F = 100 * (REKENEN_1F + REKENEN_1S) / rekenen_n,
    math_1S = 100 * REKENEN_1S / rekenen_n,
    reading_1F = 100 * (LV_1F + LV_2F) / reading_n,
    reading_2F = 100 * LV_2F / reading_n
    #DUO only count each pupil once, so to get the totals for reaching 1F in both reading and math, you must also count         the pupils that reached 1S and 2F
  ) |>
  filter(rekenen_n > 0, reading_n > 0)
    #filter out schools where no pupils are counted for maths and reading, this might not occur for Amstelveen, but is          necessary for calculating averages.

#calculate Schoolweging
school_weights <- schoolweging |>
  mutate(INSTELLINGSCODE = str_remove(OVT, "\\|.*$")) |>
  group_by(INSTELLINGSCODE) |>
  summarise(schoolweging = weighted.mean(schoolweging, w = aantal_leerlingen),
    .groups = "drop")

#Combine reference-level results with schoolweging
school_data <- left_join(ref_levels, school_weights, by = "INSTELLINGSCODE")

#Amstelveen Gemeente
amstelveen_data <- filter(school_data, GEMEENTENAAM == "Amstelveen")

#Final data
amstelveen_data |>
  select(INSTELLINGSNAAM_VESTIGING, schoolweging,
          math_1F, math_1S, reading_1F, reading_2F)

```

```{r}
school_data |>

#check all percentages
```

```{r filter-converse}
# all Dutch schools, one row per school per level
final_data <- school_data |>
  filter(!is.na(schoolweging)) |>
  select(INSTELLINGSNAAM_VESTIGING, GEMEENTENAAM, schoolweging,
         rekenen_n, reading_n,
         math_1F, math_1S, reading_1F, reading_2F) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(math_1F, math_1S, reading_1F, reading_2F),
    names_to = "level",
    values_to = "percentage"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    subject = if_else(str_starts(level, "math"), "Maths", "Reading"),
    type = if_else(str_ends(level, "1F"),
                   "Basic level (1F)",
                   "Target level (1S / 2F)"),
    n_students = if_else(subject == "Maths", rekenen_n, reading_n)
  )

#check if filter and conversion was succesful, are school with no schoolweging really filtered out and is nrow(final_data) x 4 times this amount
count(final_data, level, subject, type)
nrow(final_data)
```
```{r benchmark-regression}
# expected % based on school weighting (all Dutch schools, weighted by
# number of pupils) (regression line); for 1F the benchmark is the fixed 85% norm
final_data <- final_data |>
  group_by(level) |>
  mutate(
    expected = predict(lm(percentage ~ schoolweging, weights = n_students)),
    benchmark = if_else(type == "Basic level (1F)", 85, expected),
    diff = percentage - benchmark
  ) |>
  ungroup()

# check
final_data |>
  group_by(level) |>
  summarise(
    mean_diff = weighted.mean(diff, n_students),
    below = sum(diff < 0)
  )
# 2F and 1S should be near zero, it is a weighted (so takes into account number of students) regression line, so runs through weighted middle of the data.  middle
# remember: regression line = average that moves along with the schoolweging
```
Maths norm much harder to reach than reading.

```{r split-data-per-layer}
# grey background: all Dutch schools
# national <- final_data coded out, the grey dots were messy

# the municipality we highlight
municipality <- "Amstelveen"

muni_data <- final_data |>
  filter(GEMEENTENAAM == municipality) |>
  mutate(passed = if_else(percentage >= 85, "Yes", "No"))

# Amstelveen dots, split per row of the plot (each gets its own colours)
muni_1f <- filter(muni_data, type == "Basic level (1F)")
muni_target <- filter(muni_data, type == "Target level (1S / 2F)")

# regression line: all Dutch schools, only the target levels
national_target <- filter(final_data, type == "Target level (1S / 2F)")

# 85% norm line: one row per 1F panel
norm_1f <- distinct(muni_1f, type, subject)
```

```{r names-in-plot}
# names in the plot: all schools in the 1S / 2F panels, and only the
# schools below the 85% norm in the 1F panels
label_data <- muni_data |>
  filter(
    type == "Target level (1S / 2F)" |
      (type == "Basic level (1F)" & passed == "No")
  ) |>
  mutate(label = if_else(
    type == "Basic level (1F)",
    paste0(INSTELLINGSNAAM_VESTIGING, "\n", round(percentage, 2), "%"),
    INSTELLINGSNAAM_VESTIGING
  ))

# school name with its school weighting, for the y-axis
muni_target <- muni_target |>
  mutate(school_label = paste0(
    INSTELLINGSNAAM_VESTIGING, " (SW ", round(schoolweging), ")"
  ))
```

```{r scatter-2x2, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 8}
ggplot(mapping = aes(x = schoolweging, y = percentage)) +
  # 1F panels: the Inspectorate's fixed 85% norm
  geom_hline(data = norm_1f, aes(yintercept = 85),
             color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.8) +
  # 1S/2F panels: expected % for schools with similar pupils,
  # fitted on all Dutch schools and weighted by number of pupils
  geom_smooth(data = national_target, aes(weight = n_students),
              method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE,
              linetype = "dashed", color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.8) +
   # 1F dots: green = meets the 85% norm, red = below it
  geom_point(data = muni_1f, aes(fill = passed, size = n_students),
             shape = 21, color = "white", stroke = 0.4, alpha = 0.9) +
  # 1S/2F dots: colour shows the difference from the expected %
  # white halo behind the 1S/2F dots, so overlapping dots stay separate
  geom_point(data = muni_target, aes(size = n_students),
             color = "white", stroke = 1.2) +
  geom_point(data = muni_target, aes(color = diff, size = n_students),
             alpha = 0.75) +
    # names below the 85% norm: to the right of the dot, below the line
  geom_text_repel(data = filter(label_data, type == "Basic level (1F)"),
                  aes(label = label), size = 2.8, lineheight = 0.9,
                  nudge_x = 1, nudge_y = -1, hjust = 0, direction = "y",
                  segment.color = NA, seed = 1) +
  # names of all schools in the 1S / 2F panels
  geom_text_repel(data = filter(label_data, type != "Basic level (1F)"),
                  aes(label = label), size = 2.4, max.overlaps = Inf,
                  box.padding = 0.3, min.segment.length = 0.3,
                  segment.color = "grey60", segment.size = 0.3, seed = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Yes" = "#009E73", "No" = "#B2182B"),
    name = "Meets 85% norm"
  ) +
  scale_color_gradient2(
    low = "#B2182B", mid = "grey85", high = "#009E73", midpoint = 0,
    limits = c(-30, 30), oob = scales::squish,
    name = "Difference from\nexpected (%-points)"
  ) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 4, name = "Pupils tested") +
  facet_grid(
    type ~ subject,
    scales = "free_y",
    labeller = labeller(type = c( #add line break
      "Basic level (1F)" = "Basic level\n(1F)",
      "Target level (1S / 2F)" = "Target level\n(1S / 2F)"
    ))
  ) +
  # order of the legends: 1F colours, 1S/2F colours, dot size and determine size
  guides(
    fill = guide_legend(order = 1, override.aes = list(size = 4)),
    size = guide_legend(order = 2),
    color = guide_colorbar(order = 3),
  ) +
  # zoom in on the Amstelveen schools; the line still uses all schools
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(21, 35)) +
  theme(strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0)) #display text horizontally
```

```{r dot-plot-one-unit-prep}
# the four columns of the plot, in this order
panel_levels <- c(
  "Maths 1F\n(vs 85% norm)", "Maths 1S\n(vs expected)",
  "Reading 1F\n(vs 85% norm)", "Reading 2F\n(vs expected)"
)

dot_data <- muni_data |>
  mutate(
    # which column the dot belongs in
    panel = case_when(
      level == "math_1F" ~ panel_levels[1],
      level == "math_1S" ~ panel_levels[2],
      level == "reading_1F" ~ panel_levels[3],
      level == "reading_2F" ~ panel_levels[4]
    ),
    panel = factor(panel, levels = panel_levels),
    # 1F: the real percentage; 1S / 2F: difference from expected
    # distance from the benchmark: 85% for 1F, expected % for 1S / 2F
    x_value = diff,
    # school name with its school weighting, for the y-axis
    school_label = paste0(
      INSTELLINGSNAAM_VESTIGING, " (", round(schoolweging), ")"
    )
  ) |>
  # sort schools by their average difference at the target levels
  group_by(school_label) |>
  mutate(order_value = mean(diff[type == "Target level (1S / 2F)"])) |>
  ungroup()

dots_1f <- filter(dot_data, type == "Basic level (1F)")
dots_target <- filter(dot_data, type == "Target level (1S / 2F)")

# reference lines: 85% norm in the 1F columns, 0 in the 1S / 2F columns
lines_1f <- distinct(dots_1f, panel) |> mutate(x = 0)
lines_target <- distinct(dots_target, panel) |> mutate(x = 0)
```

```{r dot-plot-one-unit, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 7}
plot_dots <- ggplot(
  mapping = aes(x = x_value, y = reorder(school_label, order_value))
) +
  geom_vline(data = lines_1f, aes(xintercept = x),
             color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(data = lines_target, aes(xintercept = x),
             color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.7, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(data = dots_1f, aes(fill = passed, size = n_students),
             shape = 21, color = "white", stroke = 0.4) +
  geom_point(data = dots_target, aes(color = diff, size = n_students)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Yes" = "#009E73", "No" = "#B2182B"),
                    name = "Meets 85% norm (1F)") +
  scale_color_gradient2(
    low = "#B2182B", mid = "grey85", high = "#009E73", midpoint = 0,
    limits = c(-30, 30), oob = scales::squish,
    name = "Difference from\nexpected (1S / 2F)"
  ) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 5, name = "Pupils tested") +
  guides(
    fill = guide_legend(order = 1, override.aes = list(size = 4)),
    color = guide_colorbar(order = 2),
    size = guide_legend(order = 3)
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ panel, nrow = 1, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(panel.spacing.x = unit(1.2, "lines"))

plot_dots
```

```{r dot-plot-mixed-unit-prep}
# the four columns of the plot, in this order
panel_levels <- c(
  "Maths 1F\n(% of pupils)", "Maths 1S\n(vs expected)",
  "Reading 1F\n(% of pupils)", "Reading 2F\n(vs expected)"
)

dot_data <- muni_data |>
  mutate(
    # which column the dot belongs in
    panel = case_when(
      level == "math_1F" ~ panel_levels[1],
      level == "math_1S" ~ panel_levels[2],
      level == "reading_1F" ~ panel_levels[3],
      level == "reading_2F" ~ panel_levels[4]
    ),
    panel = factor(panel, levels = panel_levels),
    # 1F: the real percentage; 1S / 2F: difference from expected
    x_value = if_else(type == "Basic level (1F)", percentage, diff),
    # school name with its school weighting, for the y-axis
    school_label = paste0(
      INSTELLINGSNAAM_VESTIGING, " (", round(schoolweging), ")"
    )
  ) |>
  # sort schools by their average difference at the target levels
  group_by(school_label) |>
  mutate(order_value = mean(diff[type == "Target level (1S / 2F)"])) |>
  ungroup()

dots_1f <- filter(dot_data, type == "Basic level (1F)")
dots_target <- filter(dot_data, type == "Target level (1S / 2F)")

# reference lines: 85% norm in the 1F columns, 0 in the 1S / 2F columns
lines_1f <- distinct(dots_1f, panel) |> mutate(x = 85)
lines_target <- distinct(dots_target, panel) |> mutate(x = 0)

# same x-axis range for maths and reading: 80-100% for 1F, -15 to +35
# for 1S / 2F (invisible points that only stretch the axes)
axis_range <- dot_data |>
  distinct(panel, type) |>
  mutate(
    xmin = if_else(type == "Basic level (1F)", 80, -15),
    xmax = if_else(type == "Basic level (1F)", 100, 35)
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(c(xmin, xmax), values_to = "x_value")
```

```{r dot-plot-mixed-unit, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 7}
plot_dots <- ggplot(
  mapping = aes(x = x_value, y = reorder(school_label, order_value))
) +
  geom_vline(data = lines_1f, aes(xintercept = x),
             color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.7) +

             color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.7, linetype = "dashed") +

  geom_blank(data = axis_range, aes(x = x_value), inherit.aes = FALSE) +

             shape = 21, color = "white", stroke = 0.4) +
  geom_point(data = dots_target, aes(color = diff, size = n_students)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Yes" = "#009E73", "No" = "#B2182B"),
                    name = "Meets 85% norm (1F)") +
  scale_color_gradient2(
    low = "#B2182B", mid = "grey85", high = "#009E73", midpoint = 0,
    limits = c(-30, 30), oob = scales::squish,
    name = "Difference from\nexpected (1S / 2F)"
  ) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 5, name = "Pupils tested") +
  guides(
    fill = guide_legend(order = 1, override.aes = list(size = 4)),
```
